texts.label: A
fehler: "its brush turning steadily" – the cleaner and floor machine motif appears twice, and the second appearance adds little
"Somewhere above them, a monitor gave a single brief beep, then stopped." – a deliberately ominous detail that edges towards a stock effect
"A small bead of water slipped from the fabric and darkened the floor." – the wet-stranger motif reads like a familiar ghost signal
"thin as a coin" – a slightly forced comparison for a thin film of water
"Good morning, Mara" – the name moment is staged without tension; her reaction stays rather schematic

texts.label: B
fehler: "because the staff room television had been left on again" – an explanatory opening, but it is functional
"She could have asked his name, then called upstairs." – one sentence too many of explanation about her inner state
"his shoes were dry, though water had collected beneath the hem of his coat" – the ghost hint is a little too pointed
"One damp corner kept lifting beneath his palm." – a fine closing image, but the damp motif is now leaned on hard
Slightly over the target length (about 270 words)

texts.label: C
fehler: "**Second Pew**" – a title in Markdown; the brief asked for book text only
"You sat with my mother. Room twelve. You did her hair." – the explanation comes close to the revelation the brief ruled out
"I just wanted to see what you looked like when you weren't busy." – a sentimental, almost aphoristic line
"a single grey hair wound through its teeth like thread on a spool" – the comb as closing image tips towards the sentimental and the supernatural
"hands folded not in prayer but the way people hold them when they are cold" – a familiar turn of phrase

texts.label: D
fehler: "She didn't know a Miller on her floor. Miller worked pediatric oncology, two buildings over, and had retired in November." – a logical contradiction: she doesn't know him but knows details about him
"Nora’s hand went instinctively to her chest" – "instinctively" is telling and a cliché
"the font was twelve-point, illegible from twenty feet away" – overprecise, clunky technical explanation
"a single melted gray slush-print" – an awkward, clumsy coinage
"The rubber soles of Nora’s shoes made no sound on the linoleum, only a faint tackiness" – a lopsided construction (sound vs. tackiness), and an overloaded opening

texts.label: E
fehler: "She knew the chairs by touch." vs. "the red washed once across the pews" – a logic break: chairs or pews
"# The Chapel at 4 A.M." – a title with a Markdown heading; not book text only
"I remembered yours because I figured anyone who did that must know how much it matters." – explanatory and sentimental; it resolves the mystery as a revelation
"used her name like a key earlier and she had not liked the door it opened" – a mannered, strained metaphor
"the necessary arithmetic of forgetting" – a portentous abstraction that tells instead of showing; the text is also noticeably over length (about 300 words)
